summary: Instagram is where almost all the audience is: Hindi videos get hundreds to over 1,000 views there, while YouTube gives almost nothing (mostly under 30 views). The best videos explain a hidden sensor behind something people see daily or a robot behaving cleverly, and they get shares and saves. The channel is new, numbers are small, and the last video (Lift door) is too fresh to judge.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about a sensor in a relatable everyday or robot situation. The title is a curiosity question in Hinglish ('X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔') with a surprising twist, like 'Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!' or 'Robot Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai?'. Short, single-sensor topics with a clear visual payoff get the most shares and saves.
doMore: Make Instagram the main platform and post the Reel there first
Open with a bold surprising claim, then the question (e.g. 'Sensor Dekhta Nahi!')
Pick one sensor tied to a robot or daily scene people recognise (robot, street light, tap, door)
Make shareable, save-worthy videos: a clear one-line takeaway or a simple circuit at the end
Reuse the top topics from new angles, such as PIR and IR sensors in new situations, and check results after 48 hours before judging
stopDoing: Near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos and two IR sensor videos split the views)
Plain 'How X works' titles or vague object-only hooks that lack a surprising claim
Expecting YouTube Shorts to grow with the same Hinglish formula without testing a YouTube-specific change
